# s296 — Print the nested relay: an orchestrator per slice, with its own contract

`slicer ai relay` describes an outer session that spawns one orchestrator subagent per slice, and a new `slicer ai relay-orchestrator` prints that orchestrator's whole contract and run report on its own, so neither text depends on a file outside slicer. Both open with one contract marker, `Contract: relay v4`, which `--json` also carries.

**Findings:** owner decision, session 2026-10-15: slicer ai relay is the main relay contract; nested-relay trials s290, s279 and idea0 S16, S03 · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-15** — Trial run 3 (2026-10-15, s293 and s301 under trial prompt v3): the Waiting bullet's 'run a role in the foreground' was not possible. In Claude Code an orchestrator's Agent tool had no foreground option, so every role ran in the background. Seen: the harness pressed orchestrators to hand back while a role ran ('[handback-send-enforce] Your report has not been delivered', 9 times in one run). Implementers reported while their own background full suite still ran. A resumed role's report went to the outer session instead of the orchestrator. Word the waiting rule as the agents repo's relay-orchestrator role (s73 branch) does: end the turn while a role runs; a nudge for the report is not a reason to report; resume a role that stopped with its own work running; every brief tells roles to run long commands in the foreground with a long timeout. See s304 for the contract version marker, which replaces this slice's '<slicer version>' marker.

## Why

The owner's `/usage` for the week of 2026-10-15 showed 68% of usage from sessions active 8+ hours and 62% at more than 150k context. The cause was one orchestrating session running slice after slice, its context near 256k. `slicer ai relay` already says to compact or start fresh between slices, but the model cannot compact itself.

Two owner trials on 2026-10-15 ran a nested shape instead: the outer session (the one the owner talks to) spawns one orchestrator subagent per slice, and the orchestrator spawns the implementer, reviewer and gate. Four slices passed and landed (slicer s290 and s279; idea0 adjudicate S16 and pitfight S03). The contract they used lived in a trial prompt outside slicer. The owner decided that `slicer ai relay` is the main relay contract and must give the full contract itself, with the orchestrator's part printed by its own command so the orchestrator never reads the outer session's steps (relay-run begin and end, landing, push). Ownership confusion between the two was the main v1 trial defect.

Trial defects this text fixes: the finish step ran before review; heartbeats overwrote a step's task text; an orchestrator kept itself alive with sleep and monitor loops and left them running after its report; no tie-break when the implementer and reviewer disagreed on a bug; agents carried no environment rules.

Folded in s304 (owner, 2026-10-15): both texts carry one contract version, `relay v4`, shared with the agents repo's `relay-orchestrator` role, so a mismatch between slicer and the role files shows. A marker with the slicer version would change on every release whether the contract changed or not. The waiting rule follows trial run 3 (see the note): an orchestrator's spawns had no foreground option.

## Files

- `src/slicer/ai.py`, a constant `RELAY_CONTRACT = 4`, with a comment saying when to bump it: a rule an outer session, orchestrator or role follows changes (order, gate, tracking order, waiting, report shape), not a rewording. The agents repo's `relay-orchestrator` role already says "contract v4", so the number starts at 4.
- `src/slicer/ai.py`, `relay_text`: its first line is `Contract: relay v4`, from `RELAY_CONTRACT`.
  - `## Roles`: the outer session talks to the owner, runs Setup, owns the relay-run, spawns one orchestrator per slice, reads only its run report, lands branches one at a time, files later notes, and writes no product code. The orchestrator runs one slice under the contract `slicer ai relay-orchestrator` prints. Where the agent cannot nest subagents, the outer session is also the orchestrator, follows that contract itself, and compacts or starts a fresh session between slices.
  - `## Setup`: two bullets. The orchestrator's agent, model and reasoning effort, set explicitly on every spawn; it runs as the agent type `relay-orchestrator` where the harness has one installed, otherwise as a general-purpose agent briefed with `slicer ai relay-orchestrator`. The environment lines every brief carries (interpreter, shell limits, scratch directory), taken from the project's own instructions.
  - `## Order`: the outer steps. Create the worktree, `relay-run begin`, record the orchestrator step. Spawn the orchestrator with a brief that starts "First run `slicer ai relay-orchestrator` and follow it.", then the environment lines, the slice, worktree and branch, roles with agent/vendor/model/reasoning, the end point, a temp directory per role, RUN and the orchestrator's step id. One slice runs in the foreground; parallel slices (disjoint files) start together and the outer session waits for their reports without polling. Check the report's first line (the contract marker) and last line ("nothing left running: yes"); without the last line, stop the orchestrator first. Mark the orchestrator step, end the run, file the report's later notes as one more commit on the slice branch, then land when authorized. Replace the compact sentence: each slice gets a fresh orchestrator.
  - Keep `## Gate`, `## Stop`, `## Close` and the roles matrix as they are. `## Every brief` gains only: every brief carries the environment lines verbatim.
- `src/slicer/ai.py`, new `orchestrator_text(finish, required_note_kind)`. Its first line is `Contract: relay v4`, from `RELAY_CONTRACT`, the same line `relay_text` starts with. Then the rules:
  - work only in the named worktree, absolute paths, never change directory, no product code, tracking through slicer commands only;
  - follow Order, Gate, Every brief and Stop of `slicer ai relay` for this one slice, with the roles the brief lists; label each agent `ID role`;
  - relay-run: a new step for every round (implement, each fix round, review, gate) with `--parent` the orchestrator step; a heartbeat passes no new `--task`; never mark its own step or end the run;
  - the closing note and the finish step run only after `VERDICT: PASS`, and every implementer brief says so;
  - waiting: spawns may run in the background with no foreground option. When a role's result is needed, end the turn and let its report wake you. A nudge to report while a role it started still runs is not a reason to report. A role that reports while a command of its own still runs, or stops waiting on its own background work, has not finished its round: resume it and tell it to finish. Send the final report once, never an interim one; before ending a turn without it, send the outer session one line saying what it waits on. No sleep loops, monitor keepalives or background shell jobs; nothing it started still runs when it reports. Every role brief says to run long commands such as the full suite in the foreground with a long timeout.
  - read thin: the implementer's report and the diff stat; the full diff or cited lines only for a finding the reviewer and architect disagree on, a finding the implementer disputes, a deviation, or a diff from a role the matrix marks for the orchestrator's own read (rule u6), which is a scope-and-honesty check before review, not a correctness review;
  - disputes: a reproduction the reviewer ran beats the implementer's "does not reproduce"; inside the slice it goes back to the implementer, outside it goes in the report as a later note;
  - gate: resume the agent that raised the blockers; a fresh reviewer only when that agent is gone or the fixes rewrote much of the diff;
  - after PASS and the finish step, commit on the slice branch if the brief allows; never merge, rebase onto main or push;
  - stop and return without asking the owner: three gate FAILs, an ambiguous or wrong spec, or an owner decision; design choices the reviewer marks as the owner's go under "Owner needed".
  Then the run report, at most 30 lines: the contract marker line, then `SLICE ... OUTCOME pass|fail|stopped BRANCH ... @ sha`, worktree, rounds and the last verdict line, tests, diff stat, deviations accepted, later notes, owner needed, role steps, and the last line `nothing left running: yes`. Harness-neutral like the rest of the relay text: no Claude Code tool names.
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: `ai relay-orchestrator`, beside `ai relay-roles`, with `--json` (`{"contract": "relay v4", "orchestrator": text}`) and `--lean`. It reads `implement_finish` and `handoff_requires_note_kind` the way `ai relay` does, and prints the generic text with a stderr warning outside a project. Read-only.
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: `ai relay --json` adds `"contract": "relay v4"` beside the text.
- `docs/commands.md`, `docs/agents.md` (the new JSON shape and the `contract` field on both), `docs/getting-started.md` where it describes `ai relay`, and `CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased]`.
- `tests/test_relay_roles.py`, beside the `test_AiRelay_*` tests.
